lead: Jacksonville plumbing deals with heat, storms, sandy soil and some of Florida's oldest neighborhoods. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Jacksonville.
risk: cast-iron drain failures, slab leaks and storm flooding
risk_short: cast-iron drains, slab leaks and flooding
why: Riverside, Avondale, Springfield and San Marco have homes from the early 1900s with cast-iron drains and clay laterals. Many mid-century homes have cast-iron drains under the slab that are rotting from the inside.
Hurricanes and nor'easters flood low areas near the St. Johns River and the beaches. Homes built from the late 1970s to the mid-1990s may have polybutylene supply pipe.
water: JEA pumps water from deep wells in the Floridan Aquifer. It is moderately hard, and treatment removes the sulfur smell that Florida well water can have.
tips: Have cast-iron drains scoped in older homes.
Shut off the main valve before a hurricane evacuation.
areas: PipeMend works in Riverside, San Marco, Avondale, Mandarin, Arlington, the Southside and every other Jacksonville neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Jacksonville Building Inspection Division, and plumbing contractors are licensed by the Florida Construction Industry Licensing Board.

faq.q: Why do older Jacksonville homes have drain problems?
faq.a: Many have cast-iron drain lines that corrode from the inside after decades of use. Slow drains, backups and sewer smells are common signs. A camera inspection shows whether lining or replacement is needed.
